## Breaking change
Configuration of the squeezebox integration through configuration.yaml is now deprecated. Please consider using the frontend to configure the squeezebox integration instead. 


## Proposed change
This moves the squeezebox integration to the configuration flow so that it can be configured from the frontend and loaded without restarting home assistant. Servers will automatically be discovered by the "discovery" integration, or by this integration once it is loaded. If the user adds this integration from frontend, it will attempt to automatically discover the server as well.

Relatedly, the squeezebox integration will now handle individual players coming online or going offline while home assistant is running. Previously, the integration would only detect players that were present during startup.

Fixed the delay - the I/O was mocked but timeout was left at 5 seconds. Added additional tests.

Also found more duplicated schema as I was going through the tests. Should be all cleaned up now.
Despite setting a `unique_id`, the "ignore" button is missing from the frontend. I can't seem to figure out why. Any thoughts?
I see that "discovery" is not in the list of sources that allow the "ignore" button to appear in the frontend. See https://github.com/home-assistant/frontend/blob/dev/src/data/config_flow.ts
Test failures are unrelated to this integration/PR - not sure how to get the tests to re-run.
Azure Pipelines successfully started running 1 pipeline(s).

If it doesn't pass, you may need to rebase
https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/development_catching_up/
Thanks. I think the remaining failure was just a timeout, but I rebased anyway.

I think there is one more use case.  

1. Setup squeezebox config entry.
2. Delete config entry
3. Add another config entry.

I'm not sure if `async_setup` will be run again so discover might not ever startup again in this instance.

Everything else is looking good at this point, I'll run though it one more time once the above is addressed or confirmed to not be an issue.

I think that use case is addressed by `start_server_discovery` in `async_setup_entry` as well as `async_setup`. `start_server_discovery` checks if server discovery is already running so we can safely call it in both places. I added that in 60b0214.

However, I realized I did introduce a bug by deleting the unused variable `now` from the definition of the player `_discovery` function in f9877dd. I forgot that `async_call_later` ends up passing this argument, so we have to be prepared to accept it. I just fixed that.

Thanks for all your help on this. I've definitely learned a lot from your code review.
Changed `await` to `asyncio.create_task` in both places `start_server_discovery` is called so that the server discovery task does not block the integration from finishing configuration.

One more use case: deleting a config entry and re-adding the same server. I needed to remove the config entry's players from the list of known players so that they would be re-detected without a restart.
No problem, I'll rework the tests.

The Squeezebox integration will now handle individual players coming online or going offline while Home Assistant is running. Previously, the integration would only detect players that were present during startup.

🙏

Thank you!

## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
Since the update to 0.111.x (observed on 0.111.1 and 0.111.3 - didn't try 0.111.0 or 0.111.2), the media_title, media_artist, media_album_name, and entity_picture are not being updated when a streaming station (Pandora, in my case) changes from one song to the next.)  The correct song information / artwork is shown in the LMS webpage and for each synced player.  Re-loading the Home Assistant web-page does not correct the discrepancy, nor does pausing and resuming play of the song in LMS.

Prior to updating to 0.111.1, I had never seen this behavior.  After restoring to a backup of my Home Assistant virtual machine from just before updating to 0.111.1, I was able to confirm that the problem does not exist on 0.110.7.  Upon switching back to 0.111.1, the problem came back.  Updating to 0.111.3 did not cause the problem to go away.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.111.1 and 0.111.3 tested / confirmed broken
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 0.110.7
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv): Home Assistant Supervised, Ubuntu 18.04.4 LTS, running on a Proxmox VM
- Integration causing this issue: Logitech Squeezebox.  My LMS setup is running Logitech Media Server Version: 7.9.2 - 1578996832 @ Tue Jan 14 12:17:56 CET 2020.  LMS is running in an Ubuntu 18.04-based container on Proxmox.
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/squeezebox/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

Integration configured in configuration.yaml as per documetation:
```yaml

 - platform: squeezebox
   host: music-serv.lan
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--

-->

No errors are logged related to LMS / Squeezebox when this happens.

comments:
Hey there @rajlaud, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`squeezebox`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L386) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Thank you for reporting this. I'm able to reproduce it. This a bug in how pysqueezebox detected updates to playlists. I fixed the issue in the latest version of pysqueezebox (v0.2.3). 

There is a pending pull request for the `squeezebox` integration (https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/35669). When that gets merged this issue will be fixed.

review_comments: `async_unload_entry` is missing here.
Does this need to be nested in `async_setup_entry`?

Yes. It is much easier for the player discovery functions to be nested - than we can use `async_call_later` without parameters. This thread is specific to the configuration entry (the individual Logitech Media Server).
Can we avoid having to set `available` from outside the object and have `async_update` check `self._player.connected` instead?

Unfortunately, no. This is a problem with how Logitech Media Server handles disconnected players. For a short period of time (a few minutes), `connected` is false. After that period of time elapses, the server forgets completely about the player, and abruptly disconnects if you attempt to query information about it.

My workaround is to stop trying to query disconnected players by having `async_update` skip them. If they are re-discovered, I mark them `connected` so we start updating them again. I check `player.connected` just in case we have rediscovered a player during the limited time it is found by the server but in the disconnected state.
We want to avoid accessing the entity from outside. We can use our dispatch helper to signal an entity method from outside.
Ok. I think this got merged before your comment, but I can create a new PR to address this and your other comments below.
Ok to patch `async_setup` and `async_setup_entry` as there isn't a good way to block setup otherwise
We should use MockConfigEntry here instead
There is a `TOCTOU` race condition here since there isn't an `asyncio.Lock` when checking to see if the discovery task is in `hass.data[DOMAIN]`
Disregard, I don't think it can actually ever happen.

Ah. If I instantiate an `asyncio.Lock` and then prefix the `if DISCOVERY_TASK` block with `async with lock:` that should remove the race condition, right? It's not hypothetical since `start_server_discovery` is getting called from both `async_setup` and `async_setup_entry`.
We don't need to handle state unavailable. It's handled by the base entity class.
We can use `dict.setdefault` here.
We can invert this check and then outdent below.
Is discovery still going to be running if all entries are deleted?

Yes. The server discovery will run if the integration is loaded. I think this behavior makes sense. For example, if the server `host`, `username`, or `password` changed, the user would delete the old entry and add a new one. It is nice to have the server discovered automatically.

Ideally we stop discovery if there are no more config entries loaded, and then restart it the next time a config entry it loaded.

This allows users to migrate from a squeezebox to some other device without restarting and having the overhead of discovery running for a device they no longer have.
Ok. The discovery task will now end on unload of the last config entry.
Thanks for fixing that.  We probably need to start it again if it’s not running when the first config entry is loaded instead of in async setup?

You're right - we need to make sure it is running when we load a config entry. One nice thing about having it start in `async_setup` is that you can load the integration manually in `configuration.yaml` with `squeezebox:` and let it auto-discover squeezeboxes (which is a good substitute for using the deprecated `discovery` integration if `squeezebox` is the only thing left in `discovery` you care about). I have it loading (if unloaded) in both places now.

I also realized the player discovery task was not cleaning up gracefully, so I fixed that too.
Why do we do this here when we do it in the platform setup too?

So that instead of loading the `discovery:` integration, you can load `squeezebox:` in `configuration.yaml` and auto-discover servers. Since `discovery` is deprecated and most other things can be discovered through `ssdp` and `zeroconf`, I thought this was useful.

I run it when setting up a config entry too, so that you automatically begin discovering squeezebox servers once you first load the integration from the UI.

`start_server_discovery` checks if server discovery is already running so we won't end up with multiple copies of this running.
We're deprecating the platform section in configuration.yaml here so we shouldn't add new features that depend on some other part of configuration.yaml.
Ok, then I will run the internal discovery for servers only if there is a current config entry. This and other suggested changes in PR #37030
We should leave the platform schema and add `cv.deprecated` so they still get validation of the yaml during the transition period.
Ah, got it. And now I see where cv.deprecated goes. Thanks.
The same `TOCTOU` race condition mentioned above exists here as well.
Disregard, I don't think it can actually ever happen.
We shouldn't patch homeassistant code, we should instead patch `pysqueezebox`
Got it. This is actually `pysqueezebox` code that I patched after import rather than as `pysqueezebox.async_discover`. Fixing to patch `pysqueezebox` directly.

Its fine as-is (actually better than patching directly since its targeted to just the one place) since the code being patched is `pysqueezebox`

For other reviewers `async_discover` is coming from `pysqueezebox`: `from pysqueezebox import Server, async_discover`
